A 0.5 kg ball is attached to a 1 m string and swings in a conical pendulum at $\theta = 45^{\circ}$. Find the period, tension, and speed. Solution: $T_{period} = 2\pi\sqrt{l\cos\theta/g} = 2\pi\sqrt{1 \times 0.707/9.8} = 2\pi\sqrt{0.0721} = 2\pi \times 0.269 = 1.69$ s. $T = mg/\cos\theta = 0.5 \times 9.8/0.707 = 6.93$ N. $r = l\sin\theta = 0.707$ m. $v = \sqrt{gr\tan\theta} = \sqrt{9.8 \times 0.707 \times 1} = 2.63$ m/s.

A conical pendulum has a period of 2 s and a string length of 1 m. Find the angle $\theta$ and the radius of the circle. Solution: $T_{period} = 2\pi\sqrt{l\cos\theta/g}$, so $2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\cos\theta/9.8}$. $(2/(2\pi))^2 = \cos\theta/9.8$. $\cos\theta = 9.8/(\pi^2) = 0.993$. $\theta = 6.8^{\circ}$. $r = 1 \times \sin 6.8^{\circ} = 0.119$ m.

A 0.2 kg mass on a 0.5 m string rotates in a horizontal circle at 3 rad/s. Find the angle, tension, and height. Solution: $\omega = \sqrt{g/(l\cos\theta)}$, so $\cos\theta = g/(l\omega^2) = 9.8/(0.5 \times 9) = 2.18$. Since this exceeds 1, the pendulum cannot maintain this angular velocity — the required angle would exceed 90 degrees. The maximum $\omega = \sqrt{g/l} = \sqrt{9.8/0.5} = 4.43$ rad/s.

Two conical pendulums: Pendulum A has length 0.8 m at $\theta = 30^{\circ}$, Pendulum B has length 0.5 m at $\theta = 45^{\circ}$. Which has the shorter period? Solution: $h_A = 0.8\cos 30^{\circ} = 0.693$ m, $h_B = 0.5\cos 45^{\circ} = 0.354$ m. $T_A = 2\pi\sqrt{0.693/9.8} = 1.67$ s, $T_B = 2\pi\sqrt{0.354/9.8} = 1.19$ s. Pendulum B has the shorter period.

A 100 g ball swings as a conical pendulum with a period of 1.5 s and string length 0.6 m. Find the angle, tension, and speed. Solution: $T_{period} = 2\pi\sqrt{l\cos\theta/g}$, so $\cos\theta = gT^2/(4\pi^2 l) = 9.8 \times 2.25/(4\pi^2 \times 0.6) = 22.05/23.69 = 0.931$. $\theta = 21.4^{\circ}$. $T = mg/\cos\theta = 0.1 \times 9.8/0.931 = 1.05$ N. $r = 0.6\sin 21.4^{\circ} = 0.217$ m. $v = 2\pi r/T = 2\pi \times 0.217/1.5 = 0.91$ m/s.
